title: DOS Discovery Office
layout_status: Conceptual visitor layout, not a surveyed DOS office

exhibits.title: 01  Statistics in everyday decisions
exhibits.body: Explore Singapore through economy, population, household and industry statistics. A useful starting point is a clear question: who, what period and which measure? Before comparing values, check the units, reference period, definitions and footnotes. This exhibit introduces the process; the decorative bars in the room are not official figures.
exhibits.activity: Your team needs population figures for a briefing. Which should you check before comparing two tables?
choices: Definitions, population coverage and reference dates
exhibits.explanation: Correct. Comparable definitions and periods are essential for a meaningful comparison.

exhibits.title: 02  Your digital services toolkit
exhibits.body: SingStat Table Builder helps you select data, customise tables and download results. Its APIs support data retrieval. The DOS digital toolkit also includes the SingStat Mobile App and Business Insights Tool for Enterprises (BITE). Try a task: find a relevant series, read its metadata and select an appropriate output for your briefing.
exhibits.activity: You need a customised table for analysis. Which tool is the best starting point?
choices: A screenshot with no source information
exhibits.explanation: Correct. Table Builder supports customised tables and downloads. Retain the source and metadata with your analysis.
exhibits.source_label: DOS Business Insights Tool for Enterprises

exhibits.title: 03  A common statistical language
exhibits.body: Singapore Standard Industrial Classification (SSIC) groups economic activities. Singapore Standard Occupational Classification (SSOC) groups occupations. They answer different questions: what an organisation does, and what work a person performs. Use the relevant definitions and edition when classifying records or comparing datasets.
exhibits.activity: You are classifying a person's occupation, rather than their employer's industry. Which classification applies?
exhibits.explanation: Correct. SSOC classifies occupations. SSIC classifies economic activities.

exhibits.title: 04  From responses to statistics
exhibits.body: Surveys help DOS understand businesses and households. The Household Expenditure Survey collects information about household spending and socio-economic characteristics. Ask SingStat also directs respondents to business and price survey portals. This visitor exhibit is a learning activity; use the relevant official portal for an actual survey response.
exhibits.activity: You receive an official survey invitation. Where should you submit the real response?
choices: Through the relevant official survey channel
exhibits.explanation: Correct. This walkthrough does not collect survey returns or personal information.
